notes:
Checked 2026-11-05. Tier rule: smallest bracket among 8/16/24/32/64 GB that holds memory_gb; anything above 64 GB is '128gb+' (so 12 GB cards sit in '16gb', 36 GB Macs in '64gb', 96 GB in '128gb+'). ILS prices are values read from the opened product/list pages on 2026-11-05 (incl. VAT as shown); Ivory pages say 'prices valid until 05/11/2026' and most GPUs were marked NOT AVAILABLE - the price is a list price, not a buyable one. A search-result summary gave a wrong Zap price (5060 Ti 'from 1,900' vs 3,540 on the page), so all prices come from fetched pages; Zap list entries for Apple/GMKtec were read from list pages. Speeds are not comparable across rows: hardware-corner uses Qwen3/gpt-oss at 4k context (March 2026 page), the Apple rows use llama.cpp's classic Llama 7B pp512/tg128 table, DGX Spark/Strix Halo use gpt-oss-120B pp2048/tg32. Hardware-corner pages mostly do not state a llama.cpp build. LocalScore is a crowd-sourced leaderboard and sometimes disagrees strongly (RTX 5090 66 vs 200 tok/s). 'fits' with grade E is our own size arithmetic. Apple's lineup in the Israeli listings now includes M5 Pro/Max/Ultra and 'M6' minis (iDigital and Zap) - the brief's M4/M3 Ultra parts are shown as older rows. No official USD MSRP page was opened: MSRPs come from Wikipedia (grade D); null where none was seen.

Top-up 2026-11-05: Top-up for the 21-row index; checked 2026-11-05. 29 new rows, built to the same row shape as local-ai-hardware.json. Method: Israeli prices were read from opened Zap model pages (price comparison, grade D), store pages reached through Zap's redirects (1pc.co.il, cell-tec.co.il, pccenter.co.il, mac-kanyon.co.il - grade C) and Ivory product pages (grade C). Zap model pages show no price-update date (only the date the model was added to Zap), so every Zap price is 'seen 2026-11-05'. Zap 'lowest offer' can be a seller with a 7-10 business-day delivery; Eilat in-store-only offers are recorded in the note, never as the price. Prices are what the pages showed, not stock confirmations. Speeds: llama.cpp's own 'Performance of llama.cpp on ...' discussions (CUDA #15013, ROCm #15021, Vulkan #10879, SYCL #23313, Apple #4167, Snapdragon #8273, Arm #30069) - community-submitted Llama 2 7B Q4_0 pp512/tg128 rows, graded C like the existing Apple rows; scoreboard rows are undated, different submitters use different builds, so rows are not comparable across thread types. hardware-corner pages (grade D) add Qwen3 / gpt-oss numbers for NVIDIA cards. Vendor figures (NVIDIA Orin Nano blog, Hailo model zoo) are grade C. Where a speed was measured on a sibling machine (DGX Spark for the ASUS GX10, Surface Laptop 7 for the OmniBook X 14, platform rows for Strix Halo machines, other laptops for the CPU-only row) the row says so. MSRPs come from Wikipedia (grade D). 'fits' marked grade E is our own size arithmetic. Not reachable: iDigital collections for MacBook Air / Mac Studio / Mac mini (HTTP 429), KSP (403), CNX Software, Phoronix and OpenBenchmarking (403), justine.lol (connection refused), amd.com blog (timeout). WebSearch used 6 of the 10 allowed calls. Two suggestions for existing rows: the ASUS ROG Flow Z13 128GB is 14,990 at Priority Computers on Zap (index row has Bug 15,103); the RTX 5060 8GB row can take Zap's 1,990.
